differential.name: Metabolic-vascular syndrome (hypertension, insulin resistance, atherogenic dyslipidaemia)

supporting_evidence.finding: Documented diagnosis of hypertension and prescription of antihypertensive agents
Elevated LDL‑C (190 mg/dL) and triglycerides (210 mg/dL)
Random glucose 180 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.2 %
BMI >30 kg/m² noted in recent vitals

differential.reasoning: The combination of hypertension, insulin resistance (elevated glucose/A1c), and atherogenic dyslipidaemia fulfills criteria for metabolic‑vascular syndrome, which explains the patient’s cardiovascular risk profile.

differential.name: Sub‑clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)

supporting_evidence.finding: Markedly elevated LDL‑C (190 mg/dL)
Family history of premature coronary artery disease
10‑year ASCVD risk >10 % based on available variables

differential.reasoning: High LDL‑C together with hypertension and diabetes places the patient at significant risk for sub‑clinical atherosclerosis, even though imaging has not yet been performed.

differential.name: Intermittent/poorly controlled type‑2 diabetes mellitus

supporting_evidence.finding: Random glucose 180 mg/dL
HbA1c 7.2 %
Prescription for metformin without recent glucose trend data

differential.reasoning: Elevated glucose values and HbA1c indicate diabetes that may be intermittently uncontrolled, possibly due to medication non‑adherence or lifestyle factors.

differential.name: Resistant hypertension

supporting_evidence.finding: Patient is on three antihypertensive agents (ACE‑I, thiazide, calcium‑channel blocker)
No documented blood‑pressure readings in the record

differential.reasoning: The medication regimen suggests resistant hypertension, but lack of documented BP values makes confirmation uncertain.

differential.name: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)

supporting_evidence.finding: BMI >30 kg/m² and reported habitual snoring
No polysomnography performed

differential.reasoning: Obesity and snoring raise suspicion for OSA, yet objective testing is absent, limiting confidence.

differential.name: Non‑alcoholic fatty liver disease / NASH

supporting_evidence.finding: Metabolic syndrome components (obesity, diabetes, dyslipidaemia)
No liver enzymes reported; imaging not performed

differential.reasoning: The metabolic milieu predisposes to NAFLD/NASH, but lack of hepatic labs or imaging makes the diagnosis speculative.

differential.name: Major depressive disorder / adjustment disorder

supporting_evidence.finding: Patient reports recent psychosocial stressors and low mood
No PHQ‑9 or GAD‑7 screening completed

differential.reasoning: Stressors and mood symptoms suggest possible depressive or adjustment disorder, but formal screening is missing.

differential.name: Early chronic kidney disease (tubular dysfunction)

supporting_evidence.finding: Borderline hyperkalemia (5.3 mmol/L) with normal creatinine
No urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio available

differential.reasoning: Isolated potassium elevation may hint at early tubular dysfunction, yet insufficient renal data precludes a firm diagnosis.

primary_diagnosis: Metabolic-vascular syndrome (hypertension, insulin resistance, atherogenic dyslipidaemia)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient exhibits classic features of metabolic‑vascular syndrome: hypertension, insulin resistance, and atherogenic dyslipidaemia. These inter‑related abnormalities drive the elevated cardiovascular risk captured by sub‑clinical ASCVD and intermittent diabetes control. While resistant hypertension, OSA, NAFLD, mood disorder, and early CKD are plausible contributors, each lacks definitive objective data, rendering their probabilities lower. The differential reflects the hierarchy of evidence‑based likelihoods while acknowledging unresolved findings that require further workup.
unresolved_findings: Extremely high PDW 271.7 fL (likely lab artifact)
Normal hemoglobin despite chronic anemia code
Borderline hyperkalemia with normal renal function
Single random glucose and A1c without trend
No fasting lipid repeat after lifestyle/medication change
No liver function tests or imaging
No sleep study or STOP‑BANG assessment
recommended_workup: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring or home BP log to confirm resistant hypertension
Repeat fasting lipid panel after 3 months of therapy
Serial HbA1c and fasting glucose to assess diabetes control
Polysomnography or home sleep apnea testing
Abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan for NAFLD/NASH evaluation
Coronary artery calcium scoring or carotid duplex ultrasound for sub‑clinical ASCVD
Urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio and repeat basic metabolic panel
Complete blood count to verify anemia status
PHQ‑9 and GAD‑7 questionnaires for mood and anxiety screening
Review medication adherence (pill counts, pharmacy refill data)
